vocabulary_sources.model_tone: NONE. The model exposes no BD TONE control at a86cf9c4. TONE is therefore a reference-side axis only: ours is rendered at its single setting and compared with recordings taken at other TONE positions. perceptual_gate notes BD's TONE neighbour moves the 808's pitch by 0.1 cents, so TONE conditions test whether the glide target holds across TONE, not a TONE control of ours.

conditions.selection_rule: Candidates are selected (and any parameter grid read) on DEVELOPMENT only. UNTOUCHED is evaluated once per selected candidate and never used to choose between candidates.

development.why: the gate's own BD target (model/drum_verify.py REF_MAIN)
accent exists only in MARS; model DECAY for a MARS letter is unmapped, so the accent metric is differential (below)
second hit at 300 ms = pitch_trajectory.ANALYSIS_S, so the first hit's analysed span is complete

untouched.why: second hit while the first is ~7 dB down (tau 142 ms): heavier interference than development

the only untouched ACCENT LEVEL available: the BD recordings carry two accent levels (A, B), both needed by the differential metric, so accent LEVELS cannot be held out with a reference -- only the MARS cells can. 2.0 (ACCENT_MAP C) has no BD recording.

limits_of_this_split: Accent levels with a reference cannot be held out (two levels exist, both used); the held-out accent evidence is MARS cells A01/E05/F06 plus one reference-less model condition at 2.0.
Retrigger has no recording on either corpus (single hits only). Retrigger conditions therefore carry no pass bar on glide: a bar there would be calibrated on our own model.
MARS DECAY letters are not mapped to our DECAY knob; the accent metric is a within-cell difference so that unmapped offset cancels to first order. That cancellation is an assumption, labelled here.

The axis-held-out guard is satisfied on ACCENT only by MARS cells A01/E05/F06 (cell, not level) and by U-R300-D50-A2, a reference-less condition with no bar: the new accent LEVEL measures nothing against the 808. The guard does not require a held-out value to sit on a condition that carries a bar; this is stated rather than enforced (PR #601 review, rule 8).

primary_metric.name: untouched_median_abs_glide_deficit_cents
primary_metric.per_condition: d_c = glide_cents(reference_c) - glide_cents(ours_c), each measured exactly as tools/bd_pitch_baseline.py::measure does (perceptual_gate condition(), F_REF, onset at the gate's convention); this is the baseline JSON's glide_deficit_cents
primary_metric.aggregate: median over UNTOUCHED Fischer conditions of |d_c|
primary_metric.pass: improvement >= minimum_improvement (below), AND the per_condition_no_worsening guard holds on every MEASURED untouched Fischer condition (refused_readings below), AND no candidate refusal; raw d_c for every condition, and the excluded list, are reported beside any ratio
primary_metric.why_glide: glide_cents is early-window minus late-window of ONE trajectory, so a constant tuning shift cannot move it (qualified in tools/test_pitch_trajectory.py), and both windows start after 10 ms, so the 4 ms attack retune cannot be read as glide

onset_phase_known_answer.finding: glide_cents reads onset phase: a constant-pitch decaying sinusoid (true glide 0) reads more glide with a cos-phase onset than a sin-phase one (phase_only = |cos - sin|). Same class as #558's finding for the gate's pitch_shape (~37 cents).

scope.basis: every DECAY knob a Fischer condition of this record uses (development and untouched), minus unqualified_knobs (0.0, excluded by refused_readings). The aggregate itself sees only the untouched knobs 5, 7.5 and 10; 2.5 is development-only.
scope.tool: tools/bd_glide_phase_sweep.py (default mode); F_REF 52 Hz as tools/bd_pitch_baseline.py

onset_phase_known_answer.consequence: within the scope above, every cell is below the rule's apparatus part, 2 x 13.9 = 27.8 cents, so an onset-phase change ALONE cannot satisfy the rule at a declared condition; margin 27.8 / 13.63 = 2.04x. The worst cell is within 0.3 c of the single-reading floor (13.9), so a candidate that changes the resonator's numerator or onset phase must report this term beside its improvement. This claim is about the declared knobs only; see range_wide.

range_wide.grid: DECAY knobs 0..10 in 0.1 steps x f0 40..65 Hz in 0.5 Hz steps x 48 and 44.1 kHz: 10302 cells, 513 refused (python3 tools/bd_glide_phase_sweep.py range --jobs 3, 1 min 38 s)
range_wide.statement: Over the whole DECAY range the onset-phase term is NOT bounded by the apparatus part: at knob 0.6, 52 Hz, 48 kHz it is 34.21 c (sin -68.2, cos -34.0). Knob 0.7 reaches 27.06 c and 0.5 26.65 c. From knob 0.9 up it is below 20.2 c and falls monotonically to 9.45 c at knob 10. No condition of this record sits at knobs 0.1-0.9.
range_wide.test_probe: tools/bd_glide_phase_sweep.py::EDGE_PROBE (knobs 0-1 step 0.1, 50-54 Hz, 48 kHz) is recomputed by the test; a range-wide figure below it fails

onset_phase_known_answer.edge_finding: FINDING (#602, not fixed here): just above its refusal threshold glide_cents ANSWERS with readings tens of cents wrong instead of refusing. At knob 0.6 / 52 Hz / 48 kHz a true-zero glide reads -68.2 c; at knob 0, which refuses on 94 of 102 fine-grid cells, the 8 cells it answers (48 kHz, 40-43.5 Hz) read +76 to +97 c. Its MIN_FRAMES = 3 late-window precondition is asserted too loosely. Hence unqualified_knobs in refused_readings.
onset_phase_known_answer.abs_error_caveat: with F_REF fixed at 52 Hz the reading of a true-zero glide depends on f0: at the scoped knobs up to 59.25 c (knob 2.5, 40 Hz, 48 kHz) over 40-65 Hz, and up to 15.66 c within 48-56 Hz. It cancels in d_c only if the 808 and ours sit at the same f0; the 13.9 c floor was measured near 50 Hz and does not cover it. Filed with the edge finding (#602).

refused_readings.why: glide_cents is not qualified at DECAY knob 0 (Q 2.3, tau ~15 ms): on the fine grid (f0 40-65 Hz in 0.5 Hz steps, 48 and 44.1 kHz) the closed-form known answer REFUSES on 94 of 102 cells, and the 8 cells it answers (48 kHz, 40-43.5 Hz) read +76 to +97 cents for a true-zero glide (#602). Two untouched Fischer conditions sit at knob 0. Declared here, before candidates exist, so that what a refusal or an unqualified reading does to the median is not chosen afterwards (PR #601 reviews).
refused_readings.unqualified_why: a condition at an unqualified knob is EXCLUDED from both medians whatever it reads, and listed: a number there is not a reading. Knob 0 is the only declared Fischer knob where the fine-grid sweep refuses any cell or reads a phase term at or above the apparatus part.
refused_readings.reading: only a finite real number is a reading. A Refused, None, NaN, inf, bool or string (even "0") is REFUSED. A refusal is NEVER converted to a number: never a 0-cent reading, never a 0-cent |d_c|.
refused_readings.exclude: a condition whose REFERENCE or SHIPPED reading is REFUSED is excluded from BOTH the shipped and the candidate median (the two medians are always over the same set), and is listed by id with the side that refused.
refused_readings.candidate_refusal: a condition whose reference and shipped readings are measured but whose CANDIDATE reading is REFUSED is a FAILURE of the candidate (it made a measurable trajectory unmeasurable). It is not excluded and no candidate median is formed.
refused_readings.min_measured_why: 8 untouched Fischer conditions minus the 2 predicted refusals (the conditions at unqualified knobs); check() pins min_measured_conditions to exactly that derivation. Losing any further condition means the aggregate rests on a set nobody declared before candidates existed.
refused_readings.held_out_after_exclusion: the measured set must still contain a TONE value and a DECAY value that development never used (with the 2 predicted refusals excluded, DECAY stays held out through 75 and 10, TONE through 75, 00 and 10).
refused_readings.too_few_outcome: REFUSED: no improvement is claimed, pass or fail, and the result is reported as REFUSED with the excluded list. It is NEVER a pass. The minimum is not lowered to admit a result.
refused_readings.prediction_basis: closed-form known answer only (no Fischer or MARS file was read). These are exactly the untouched Fischer conditions at unqualified_knobs, and they are excluded whether or not the 808's or our knob-0 render happens to measure.

minimum_improvement.units: cents of reduction in the primary aggregate
minimum_improvement.why_2x: the improvement is the difference of two glide readings of ours (shipped, candidate); each can be off by the per-reading floor, so the floor of the difference is twice it

minimum_improvement.unsatisfiable_outcome: Satisfiability is judged on the statistic acceptance uses: the SHIPPED median |d| over the measured untouched Fischer set, with refused_readings' exclusions, floor and holdout applied (tools/bd_pitch_predeclaration.py::_measured_set, shared with primary_aggregate). A candidate's median cannot go below 0, so the largest showable improvement is that shipped median; the pass rule is improvement >= minimum_improvement, so satisfiable iff shipped_median >= minimum_improvement (equality admitted). If it is below, `tools/bd_pitch_predeclaration.py min-improvement --readings` REFUSES: the defect is not resolvable above apparatus + recording variability at this estimator. That is a publishable result (acceptance bullet 7). The rule is NOT loosened to admit a repair.
minimum_improvement.one_take_diagnostic: The baseline JSON's pairs.fischer_vs_ours.glide_deficit_cents is ONE take (REF_MAIN BD5050, a DEVELOPMENT condition). It is validated (finite real number, not bool or string) and reported as development_take_diagnostic, and decides nothing: without untouched shipped readings satisfiability is not claimed either way and `min-improvement` REFUSES to claim it (PR #601 third review: a one-take deficit both rejected a satisfiable experiment and passed an unsatisfiable one).
minimum_improvement.input_validation: Every baseline value is a finite real number (bool, strings such as "100", None, NaN and inf REFUSE); recording_glide_spread_cents is a magnitude and REFUSES when negative; the evaluated threshold must be finite and > 0. Missing or malformed fields REFUSE with exit 2, never a traceback or an answer. Controls: tools/test_bd_pitch_predeclaration.py::test_cli_refuses_malformed_baseline_values (the Judge's four inputs), test_cli_refuses_malformed_baseline_fields, test_cli_refuses_non_positive_threshold.

terms.why: the target against itself through candidate_path: what the gate cannot distinguish

preservation.measures: perceptual_gate.loudness_db on the UNCONDITIONED render (the gate's condition() normalises to -23, so every gate feature is BLIND to level) and run_case DRUM_PLAN BD 'early/body energy'

limit.relation: |candidate - shipped| <= limit for early/body energy (the measured quantity) and for loudness_db (BORROWED bound: no loudness repeat spread is measured)

preservation.measures: perceptual_gate feature 'attack' (5/20/50 % cumulative-energy times, first 100 ms) and the 4 ms attack retune's coefficient writes

preservation.caveat: #558 (docs/scorecard/tom-conga-558/README.md) measured that `impulse` for all six toms/congas AND BD is dominated by the gate's 44.1 -> 48 kHz rate path, not by the sound. The limit here is a DIFFERENCE (candidate - shipped through the same path against the same take), so the common rate-path term cancels to first order; whether `impulse` can see a real BD click change through that path is #588's question. test_click_moves_impulse shows a seeded click is seen.

no_parameter_statement: No repair mechanism and no parameter is proposed in this record, so no docs/sensitivity/registry.json entry is added. The first proposal of a parameter (e.g. a pitch-sigh depth or time constant) must add its registry record, grid and independent prediction BEFORE any value is selected, and list it here with registry_record.
